drafted_from: tool:read-post-calendar's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Show what this person is posting between two times, and which drafts have no time yet, so a post can be given a time or moved to another", with {"from":"2026-10-01T00:00:00Z","to":"2026-11-01T00:00:00Z"}. It runs tool:read-post-calendar and answers {"from":"2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z","to":"2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z","posts":[],"unscheduled":[]}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and keeps only its own rows (post) through the records door.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Show what this person is posting between two times, and which drafts have no time yet, so a post can be given a time or moved to another", and give it from (The start of the span, like 2026-10-01T00:00:00-04:00); to (The end of the span, after from).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:read-post-calendar and its input (the worked example shows one).
3. Read what comes back: Give from and to (dates and times with their zone).
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: post (records:list).
